close_reason: Added #[non_exhaustive] to all 8 public data-carrier structs called out in the issue: LintParameter (lib.rs), Finding (lib.rs), Deviation (deviation.rs), DeviationScope (deviation.rs), DeviatedFinding (deviation.rs), EvaluationReport (report.rs), ResolvedProfile (oscal/profile.rs), ParameterOverride (oscal/profile.rs). Added validating/ergonomic constructors where they did not exist: LintParameter::new(id, label, default_value), Finding::new(...) + with_cert_index + with_cert_sha256, Deviation::new(...) + with_effective_start + with_effective_end + with_evidence_uri, ResolvedProfile::new, ParameterOverride::new. DeviationScope already had constructors (any/issuer_dn_contains/issuer_dn_exact/serial_range); EvaluationReport already had ::new. Updated the deviation.rs module-level doctest to use Deviation::new + with_effective_end + with_evidence_uri instead of struct-literal syntax (which would fail compilation in external crates with #[non_exhaustive]). The DeviatedFinding struct deliberately ships without a constructor — it is an engine-output type produced by DeviationRunner, never user-constructed; #[non_exhaustive] documents this role and keeps the door open for future per-deviation provenance fields. Workspace tests pass; clippy --workspace --all-features clean. The single highest-leverage API-contract fix available pre-1.0 — future additions to any of these 8 structs are now non-breaking.
description:
The following public structs have one or more public fields and are NOT
marked #[non_exhaustive], which means adding any field is a breaking change:

  pkix-lint/src/lib.rs
    - LintParameter (pub id, pub label, pub default_value) — doc explicitly
      mentions OSCAL's richer parameter shape (constraint, guideline, select,
      link) is 'not modelled here'. Adding any of those becomes a major bump.
    - Finding (pub lint_id, pub citation, pub rule_bundle_version, pub result,
      pub cert_index, pub evaluated_at_unix, pub cert_sha256) — the doc itself
      anticipates 'future evidence-pack consumers would pair this finding with
      a separate per-chain hash list' and that '#[non_exhaustive]' is
      desired (PKIX-hy2e.21 amplifies this). Adding fields like
      path_position, severity_actual, evidence_chain_sha256 each becomes a
      semver-major bump.

  pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs
    - Deviation (pub id, target_lint, scope, effective_start, effective_end,
      action, justification, authorized_by, evidence_uri) — the evidence_uri
      field was added in the diff under review without a major bump because
      DeviationAddError was already #[non_exhaustive]; but the struct itself
      is not. Adding (e.g.) revoked_at or supersedes_id is breaking.
    - DeviationScope (pub kind, pub props) — the entire design rationale is
      'open-ended extensibility' (line 315) but the struct itself prevents
      adding fields. Future caching/normalization fields locked out.
    - DeviatedFinding (pub lint_id, citation, original_result, deviation_id,
      action, justification, evidence_uri, cert_index, evaluated_at_unix) —
      same exposure as Finding.

  pkix-lint/src/report.rs
    - EvaluationReport (pub profile_id, profile_version, rule_bundle_version,
      chain_length, evaluated_at_unix, findings, deviated_findings) — the
      doc explicitly claims 'all field names in this struct are part of the
      public API and will not be renamed without a semver-major bump.' But
      *adding* a field is also a breaking change without #[non_exhaustive].
      Adding e.g. chain_certs_sha256 (referenced as desired in OSCAL emit
      docs at oscal/emit.rs:42-43) becomes a semver-major.

  pkix-lint/src/oscal/profile.rs
    - ResolvedProfile (pub control_ids, pub parameter_overrides) — the doc
      itself flags that OSCAL Profile model has merge.combine, modify.alters,
      back-matter that are 'not interpreted' today. Adding any future
      directive's output here is breaking.
    - ParameterOverride (pub param_id, pub value) — OSCAL parameters can
      carry constraint, guideline, etc. (mentioned in LintParameter doc).
      Locked out.

DeviationStore IS internally Vec<Deviation> with a private field — that's
fine. DeviationRunResult HAS #[non_exhaustive]. The contract gap is in
the data-carrier types above.

# Why pre-1.0 framing makes this urgent

AGENTS.md prelaunch framing (line 'Apply these frames'): 'Design for the
eventual complete shape.' These structs all anticipate future fields
in their own rustdoc. Adding #[non_exhaustive] is the standard pre-1.0
ergonomic — callers can still construct via struct literal *within the
defining crate*, and updated rust-version is 1.73 which fully supports
this attribute.

The fix: add #[non_exhaustive] to each, and provide a constructor (e.g.
Finding::new(...), Deviation::new(...)) that callers use instead of
struct-literal syntax. The constructor surface is then explicitly
governed by Result / builder semantics, and adding fields is a default
non-breaking change.

# What the caller sees if this stays as-is

A caller writing:

    let f = Finding {
        lint_id: ...,
        citation: ...,
        rule_bundle_version: ...,
        result: ...,
        cert_index: ...,
        evaluated_at_unix: ...,
        cert_sha256: ...,
    };

will fail to compile the day any new field is added. Every consumer
that constructs Finding directly (and the rustdoc encourages this — see
the test code in lib.rs:1951 and 2026 that does exactly that) has to
update their construction site. With #[non_exhaustive] the workspace
can keep adding fields with default values without breaking anyone.

This is the single highest-leverage API-contract fix available pre-1.0.
title: API contract: public structs missing #[non_exhaustive] lock fields forever
